answer: Modularity-based community detection resists sybils: partition the trust graph to maximize within-cluster edges over between-cluster edges, anchored on a labeled honest seed core. A sybil farm — a ferrous lump of dense mutual vouches — still attaches to the honest modules through only a thin plume of attack edges, so it falls out as its own community, weakly bridged to the real one. Trust weight goes only to identities inside seed-connected modules; an isolated opal of fakes, bright within but barely linked out, earns nothing.
